t1_h: The lined script, just like at the office
t1_p: Write the script in FilmSpirit or import yours. Tag the text with each category's color: cast, props, wardrobe, vehicles. FilmSpirit suggests what is likely and you decide. Breakdown sheets are generated automatically, one per scene.

q1: Do I need to install anything?
a1: No. FilmSpirit runs in the browser on your computer, tablet or phone. Sign in with your Google account and your projects follow you to any device.
a2: Yes. If the connection drops, you keep editing and exporting in the same browser; changes are saved on your device and sent automatically when you are back online.
a3: On our servers, with daily backups. They save automatically as you work. You can also archive a project and download it complete as a ZIP with all its documents.
q4: What happens when I archive a project?
a4: It becomes read-only: you can view and export it, but it doesn't count toward your plan's active project limit. Unarchive it whenever you like, if you have a free slot.
q5: Can I try it before paying?
a5: Yes. The Script plan is free and, to see everything for production, the app has the sample project “The Last Show” with all its tabs: breakdown, storyboard, shooting schedule, call sheet, budget and more. You explore it without paying and without a card. No plan has a free trial.
a6: You lose nothing. Your scripts and projects stay saved and you can view and export them. You keep editing as many as your plan allows; the rest become read-only until you archive others or upgrade again.
q7: Do the people I invite have to pay?
a7: No. They join with a free account and work on your project with the permissions you give them, using your plan features. Up to 4 people co-write a script; production teams are for Pro (30 people) and Studio (60). Indie is for one person.
a8: Sign in through the link you were given (filmspiritpro.com/r/CODE) and the code is saved to your account, or type it when you subscribe. Each account can use one code.
q9: Can I keep using Final Draft?
a9: Yes. Write wherever you like and import the .fdx file whenever you have a new draft: FilmSpirit keeps your tags and shots where the text matches.
